name: Cian Ingram
life: “I still remember carrying a paper tray that didn't cost a week's wages.” People around the downtown fountain know Cian by a small Monday habit. Cian keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I brought takeaway chips to the public bench. The birthday girl said it was her best sea view yet.
appearance: Cian has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for a loose dark braid. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. In conversation Cian counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Cian is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Cian loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To give the birthday girl a waterfront meal within reach.
family: Tamsin Leung is Cian’s stepsibling. Cian can stop the walk at any corner. Tamsin chooses the familiar route. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *A chair on the quay*, Tamsin says, “I put the chair in lost property under freight fittings.”
connections: Adriana Ingram. The old recipe and the public bench make two possible alternatives to a costly birthday meal.

reactions.response: Cian checks that the birthday guest likes the dessert before calculating the portions.
